videos.title: Expense Sits in Assembly Not Materials | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: A house built from lumber, gypsum, concrete, and glass still costs many times the value of those raw materials because the expense sits in assembly, regulation, and financing rather than in the stuff itself.

videos.title: Cotton Gin Raised Output from 1 to 50 Pounds Per Day
videos.hook: Before the cotton gin, one worker cleaned roughly a pound of fiber per day by hand; the machine that attacked only the seed-separation step raised that output by a factor of fifty almost overnight.

videos.title: Microbes Brew Protein After Animal Energy Waste Cut | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Raising animals for protein wastes most input energy on the animal’s life; microbes could brew the same molecules for far less.

videos.title: Integrated circuit printed billions of transistors on silicon | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Before the integrated circuit, adding each transistor required another hand-soldered wire; afterward, billions could be printed onto a sliver of purified sand for a few cents.

videos.title: Satellites Cost Millions for Cheap Materials | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Satellites that reach orbit often cost millions yet contain only thousands of dollars of silicon, aluminum, and electronics — the real expense sits in the process, not the atoms.

videos.title: Catalytic Converter Price Set by Platinum Scarcity | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: A catalytic converter’s price is set less by its ceramic and steel than by a few grams of platinum, palladium, and rhodium whose scarcity keeps the floor stubbornly high.

videos.title: Rail Physics Loses on Delivered Cost | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Rail moves a ton a mile with far less energy than trucks, yet the cheaper physics mode still loses on delivered cost.

videos.title: Heat and Sealed Containers Made Food Last Months | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Most food rotted before reaching armies or cities out of season until heat and sealed containers turned harvest abundance into months of usable supply at a small multiple of the raw food cost.

videos.title: Prosthetic Costs Fifty Thousand Dollars But Materials Are Fifty

videos.title: Silicon Sensors Made Photos Cost Nearly Zero | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: For a century every photograph carried a real cost in silver, chemicals, and paper; silicon sensors collapsed the marginal cost of an image to nearly zero by turning photons into charge.

videos.title: Routine Legal Documents Cost Thousands With Near-Zero Cost | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Routine legal documents costing thousands today have an Idiot Index in the thousands because their raw-material cost is essentially zero.

videos.title: Watt Isolated Condenser to Cut Fuel Use | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Newcomen engines burned coal to reheat a cylinder they had just cooled every stroke, until Watt isolated the condenser and cut fuel use by roughly three-quarters.

videos.title: Water Purification Costs Pennies But Pipes Multiply Price | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Purifying a liter of water to drinkable standards costs pennies in energy and chemicals, yet the pipes that move it often multiply the price by orders of magnitude.

videos.title: Plate Glass Cost Dominated by Grinding Before Tin Float | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Plate glass once cost many times its raw sand and lime because weeks of grinding and polishing dominated the price — until molten glass was allowed to float itself flat on tin.

videos.title: Elder Care Costs Driven Almost Entirely by Human Hours | First Principles Daily #Shorts
videos.hook: Elder care costs are driven almost entirely by human hours, leaving little room for the material-cost reductions seen in rockets or steel.
